title: Weil/Katz explanation of flat spectra of Legendre sequences along [k]P
question: For E/F_p with #E(F_p)=r prime, generator P and a nonconstant rational function g on E of small degree d (e.g. g=x, x+1, 2x, y), the normalized twisted sums X_c = r^{-1/2} * sum_{k=1}^{r-1} chi(g([k]P)) e(ck/r), c=1..r-1, satisfy |X_c| <= C(d) * sqrt(p/r) = O_d(1) (Weil-type bound for mixed character sums over E(F_p), group characters of E times a multiplicative character of g), so the periodogram |X_c|^2 has a bounded, non-exponential law; as p grows its distribution approaches a fixed law determined by the monodromy of the associated sheaf (not Exp(1)). This explains the flat-spectrum anomaly observed in ECDLP-7 E-B for chi(x), chi(y) sequences, and implies no information about k beyond what the bound allows.
rationale: PI conjecture formulated after ECDLP-7 E-B anomaly (reproduced, two seeds + PI rerun). Needs literature check (Kohel-Shparlinski type bounds; Katz equidistribution) and decisive test.
assumptions: Half-range sequences (k=1..(r-1)/2) used in E-B differ from full-range sums; the half-range DFT is an incomplete sum and needs a completion argument (adds a log factor).
Bound constant C(d) unverified; source recollection only (Kohel & Shparlinski, ANTS 2000) — not yet checked.

notes: Speculative explanation; NOT an exploitable leak claim. Distinguish: Weil bounds give deterministic square-root cancellation (less variance), which reduces, not increases, correlation with any fixed character. | ECDLP-9: For g = x, x+1, y the bounded-maximum part is SUPPORTED (max |X_c|^2 ≈ 4p/r). For degree-4/5/3x-degree functions tested (x^2+x+1, xy, x^3+2) the claim "|X_c| <= C(d) sqrt(p/r) with bounded non-Exp(1) law" in the sense of a bounded max at these sizes is REFUTED as an empirical pattern (max grows ~ ln r, Gaussian-like moments), although no Weil envelope violation was shown. The original statement is kept unchanged; the sharpened variant is HYP-80158648.
